findings.message: Requirement 3 (evict LRU entries when the remeasured same-value total would exceed a nonzero maxSize, with eviction disposal) has no test that actually exercises it. The closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`, only fills the cache exactly to maxSize and evicts nothing. Source review shows the behavior is correct. At src/index.ts:2303-2304, `this.#removeItemSize(index)` and then `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` run after `this.#moveToTail(index)` (line 2250). `#addItemSize` (lines 1774-1777) runs `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`, and `#evict` calls `dispose(oldValue, k, 'evict')` and queues disposeAfter. That queue is flushed at line 2326. The updated entry is at the tail and its size has already been removed, so it cannot evict itself. This is a test-coverage gap only.

No test covers the clause that a same-value grow pushing the total over a nonzero `maxSize` evicts LRU entries with eviction disposal. The closest test only reaches the exact limit, with no eviction: `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` / `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`. Reading the source shows the behavior is correct: `#moveToTail(index)` (src/index.ts:2250) runs before `this.#removeItemSize(index); this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (src/index.ts:2303-2304), and `#addItemSize` evicts from the head with `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` (src/index.ts:1775-1777). The spec says unexercised clauses remain source-review obligations, so this is advisory.

Requirement 3 (an over-total same-value remeasure must evict LRU entries and dispose them) has no regression test. The closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`, lands exactly on maxSize, so no eviction happens. Reading the code shows the behavior is correct. At src/index.ts:2250, `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before the new branch at src/index.ts:2303-2304 (`this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`). #addItemSize then loops `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` from the head. The updated entry's size was zeroed first and `size <= this.#maxSize` is guarded, so the updated entry is never evicted, and status.totalCalculatedSize is set after the loop. Under the spec's Verification note this clause is a source-review obligation, so this finding is advisory.

No test exercises the same-value growth path that makes the total exceed a nonzero maxSize, so eviction is never triggered. Every growth case keeps calculatedSize within maxSize: 'maxSize: 100' gives a total of 13, and the 'exact total limit' case gives 'c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })' with total 10 at maxSize 10. Source review shows the requirement is still met. src/index.ts:2250 calls '#moveToTail(index)' before src/index.ts:2303-2304 calls '#removeItemSize(index)' and then '#addItemSize(index, size, status)'. At lines 1774-1776, '#addItemSize' evicts from the head with '#evict(true)' while 'this.#calculatedSize > maxSize'. Because 'size <= this.#maxSize' and the entry's own size was already removed, the loop stops before it can evict the updated entry. Evicted entries get the normal eviction disposal and are flushed at lines 2323-2328. This is advisory only: the sealed evidence has no executable check for the eviction, disposal, or recency combination.

Requirement 3 (eviction when a same-value remeasure pushes the total over a nonzero maxSize) has no test. The closest case is 'validation, entry admission, and exact total limit', which only reaches the limit exactly: `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` / `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)` / `t.equal(c.size, 2)`. Reading the source, the clause is satisfied: `this.#moveToTail(index)` (src/index.ts:2250) runs before `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (src/index.ts:2303-2304). `#addItemSize` then runs `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` (src/index.ts:1775-1776) while the updated entry's own size is 0, so it evicts LRU entries with eviction disposal and keeps the updated entry. The spec allows source review for clauses the command doesn't exercise, but this is still a gap in the regression tests.

Requirement 3 says a same-value update whose new total exceeds a nonzero maxSize "must evict least-recently-used entries until the total fits, retaining the updated entry as most recently used. Each evicted entry must receive the existing eviction disposal behavior." No test in test/set-size-update.ts covers this. The closest case is `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(calculatedSize, 10)` and `t.equal(c.size, 2)`, which only reaches the exact limit, so nothing is evicted. The spec makes unexercised clauses source-review obligations, and source review passes: src/index.ts:2250 `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before src/index.ts:2303-2304 `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`. addItemSize loops `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` from the head, and #evict calls `this.#dispose?.(oldValue, k, 'evict')` and queues disposeAfter. The updated entry, already at the tail with its size zeroed, is never evicted because `size <= this.#maxSize`. This finding is advisory: the behavior is correct by source review but has no regression test.

No new test sets the same value while a background fetch is pending, or with `noDisposeOnSet` plus disposeAfter during a resize eviction. Source review shows the new branch sits under `} else if (!isBF) {` (src/index.ts:2297) and leaves the different-value and background-fetch paths unchanged, so the Constraint "Preserve other set and fetch paths" holds. This is noted for completeness only.

Requirement 3 says a same-value update that pushes the total over a nonzero `maxSize` "must evict least-recently-used entries until the total fits, retaining the updated entry as most recently used", and each evicted entry must get eviction disposal. No test in test/set-size-update.ts covers this. The closest case only reaches the limit exactly: `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` / `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)` / `t.equal(c.size, 2)`, so nothing is evicted. The spec's verification bullet leaves this as a source-review obligation. Source review confirms the behavior: src/index.ts:2250 `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before src/index.ts:2303-2304 `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`. The eviction loop at src/index.ts:1775-1776 (`while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`) then evicts from the head with the 'evict' disposal reason (src/index.ts:2375). It never reaches the updated tail entry, because that entry's size has already been subtracted and `size <= this.#maxSize`. This is advisory only: there is no regression guard for the eviction path.

No regression test makes a same-value update grow past a nonzero maxSize, so nothing exercises LRU eviction or the 'evict' dispose/disposeAfter path. The closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` with maxSize 10, lands exactly on the limit (`t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`) and evicts nothing. The spec accepts source review for clauses the command does not exercise, and source review shows the behavior is correct: src/index.ts:2250 `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before src/index.ts:2303-2304 `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`, and addItemSize (src/index.ts:1775-1776) `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` evicts from the head with 'evict' disposal. The updated entry stays at the tail and cannot evict itself because its size is zeroed first and `size <= this.#maxSize`. Advisory only: a regression test is missing, but the behavior is correct.

Requirement 3 says a same-value update whose new total would exceed a nonzero `maxSize` "must evict least-recently-used entries until the total fits". No test exercises this. The closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` with `maxSize: 10`, reaches the limit exactly (`t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`), so nothing is evicted. A source review of the code order finds the behaviour correct. `this.#moveToTail(index)` (src/index.ts:2250) runs before `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (src/index.ts:2303-2304). The updated entry's size is therefore zeroed while `#addItemSize` calls `this.#evict(true)` from the head, so the loop stops before reaching the updated entry, because `size <= this.#maxSize`. Each eviction goes through the `'evict'` disposal path in `#evict`. The spec allows source review for this clause, so this finding is advisory.

None of the new regression tests covers the same-value eviction requirement. The closest case, 'validation, entry admission, and exact total limit', calls `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` with `maxSize: 10` and b sized 4, so the total reaches exactly 10 and nothing is evicted. No test checks that same-value growth evicts LRU entries, keeps the updated entry as most recently used, or sends evicted entries to dispose/disposeAfter with reason 'evict'. A source review shows the behaviour is correct: `this.#moveToTail(index)` (src/index.ts:2250) runs before `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (src/index.ts:2303-2304). `#addItemSize` then loops `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` with the updated entry's size already zeroed, so it cannot evict itself while `size <= this.#maxSize`. `#evict` calls `this.#dispose?.(oldValue, k, 'evict')`, and the set path flushes `#disposed` afterwards. The spec allows clauses the command does not exercise to be source-review obligations, so this finding is advisory.

The new tests never grow a same-value entry so that the total goes over a nonzero maxSize. The closest case is `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`, which only reaches the exact limit. So MECHANICAL never exercises the Requirement 'the same-value update must evict least-recently-used entries until the total fits, retaining the updated entry as most recently used. Each evicted entry must receive the existing eviction disposal behavior.' Source review shows the code meets it: src/index.ts:2250 calls `this.#moveToTail(index)` before `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (2303-2304). `#addItemSize` loops `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`, which evicts from the head and calls `this.#dispose?.(oldValue, k, 'evict')`. The updated entry is at the tail with size zeroed, and `size <= this.#maxSize`, so the loop cannot evict it. The spec allows source review for clauses the command does not exercise, so this finding is advisory.

Same-value growth can leave eviction disposeAfter callbacks undelivered when noDisposeOnSet is true. With maxSize: 10, insert a at size 3 and b at size 4, then set the identical a to size 8 with noDisposeOnSet: true. The new call at src/index.ts:2304, "this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)", evicts b and queues its callback at src/index.ts:2378, "this.#disposed?.push([oldValue, k, 'evict'])", but src/index.ts:2323 gates delivery on "if (!noDisposeOnSet && this.#hasDisposeAfter && this.#disposed)". The callback remains queued after set returns and may never run. The applicable requirement states, "Each evicted entry must receive the existing eviction disposal behavior." Public documentation also limits noDisposeOnSet suppression to when "the entry key is still accessible within the cache" (src/index.ts:885–886); b has been removed. Drain eviction callbacks independently of replacement-disposal suppression and cover this combined resize/eviction case.

Requirement 3 says a same-value update whose new total exceeds a nonzero `maxSize` must evict LRU entries and dispose them. No test in the new file exercises that path. The closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` with `maxSize: 10`, reaches the limit exactly (`t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`) and evicts nothing. Source review shows the behavior is correct: `this.#moveToTail(index)` (src/index.ts:2250) runs before `this.#removeItemSize(index); this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (src/index.ts:2303-2304), and `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` (src/index.ts:1775-1776) evicts from the head with `this.#dispose?.(oldValue, k, 'evict')`. Because the updated entry's size has already been removed and `size <= this.#maxSize`, the loop cannot evict the updated tail entry. This is a regression-test gap only, not a behavior defect.

Same-value growth can evict entries without delivering their disposeAfter callbacks. With maxSize: 10 and a disposeAfter recorder, insert a at size 3 and b at size 4, then set a to the identical value with size: 8 and noDisposeOnSet: true. The new branch invokes "this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)" (src/index.ts:2304), evicting b and queuing "this.#disposed?.push([oldValue, k, 'evict'])" (2378). However, "if (!noDisposeOnSet && this.#hasDisposeAfter && this.#disposed)" (2323) skips delivery, leaving b's callback pending after set returns. This violates "Each evicted entry must receive the existing eviction disposal behavior" (spec.md:20); the documented suppression applies when "the entry key is still accessible within the cache" (src/index.ts:885–886), whereas b has been removed. Drain eviction callbacks independently of replacement-disposal suppression and cover this combination.

The closest test fills the limit exactly, so nothing is evicted: `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)` and `t.equal(c.size, 2)`. Reading the source shows the behavior is correct. src/index.ts:2250 calls `this.#moveToTail(index)` before the resize. src/index.ts:2303-2304 call `this.#removeItemSize(index)` and then `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`. src/index.ts:1775-1776 then run `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`. Together these evict from the head while the updated entry stays at the tail, and `#disposed` is flushed at src/index.ts:2323-2328. The spec allows this clause to be checked by source review, so this finding is advisory.

For example, with maxSize: 10 and entries sized 3 and 7, resizing the first to 4 evicts the second. src/index.ts:2304 calls "this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)"; src/index.ts:2378 queues "this.#disposed?.push([oldValue, k, 'evict'])", but src/index.ts:2323 guards delivery with "if (!noDisposeOnSet && this.#hasDisposeAfter && this.#disposed)".
